claims.text: Equiatomic FeCoNiAl contains approximately 25 at.% each of Fe, Co, Ni, and Al.
Equiatomic FeCoNiAl has configurational entropy of at least 1.0R.
The initial equiatomic FeCoNiAl alloy is predominantly disordered fcc.
Annealing FeCoNiAl at 600–700 °C for 1–5 hours with optimized cooling can produce nanoscale B2 ordering without complete phase transformation.
The resulting mediator will consist of nanoscale B2-ordered precipitates dispersed in a disordered fcc matrix.
Al incorporation promotes local chemical ordering in FeCoNiAl.
Al-induced local chemical ordering leads to B2-ordered domains.
The B2-ordered domains have lower symmetry than the surrounding fcc matrix.
Nanoscale B2 domains enhance magnetocrystalline anisotropy.
Nanoscale B2 domains act as pinning centers for magnetic domain walls.
Enhanced magnetocrystalline anisotropy and domain-wall pinning increase coercivity relative to a homogeneous fcc phase.
Optimized FeCoNiAl may exhibit at least twice the coercivity of equiatomic FeCoNi.
Optimized FeCoNiAl will retain high saturation magnetization while its coercivity increases.
Equiatomic FeCoNi without Al addition and controlled annealing displays soft ferromagnetism with low coercivity.
The intervention is effective only over a narrow window of annealing temperature, duration, and cooling rate.
Excessive annealing temperature or duration, or improper cooling, can cause extensive phase transformation or undesired phase formation.
Extensive transformation or undesired phases may reduce saturation magnetization or alloy stability.

contradictions.description: The initial state is already defined as equiatomic FeCoNiAl, whereas the intervention includes introducing Al into FeCoNi; this makes the temporal starting point of the intervention inconsistent.
